_source: docs/backend/baseline-audit.sql run read-only in the Supabase SQL editor of the deployed HALO project
_contents: catalog only: table and column definitions, RLS flags, policies, foreign keys, functions, privileges, triggers, extensions, roles. No rows from any HALO table, no passwords, no keys.
_findings: server_version_num 170006 = PostgreSQL 17.6. The local test suite runs on PGlite/Postgres 18.

ucmr5_utilities has RLS enabled with a single SELECT policy named 'Allow public read access on ucmr5_utilities' using (true). The anon/authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants are inert under RLS. The guarded remedy in YOUR_TODO 1.1 was NOT needed and was NOT run.
The reconstruction had guessed that policy's name as 'Enable read access for all users'; no deployed policy ever had that name. Corrected in reconstructed_baseline.sql and in the YOUR_TODO remedy.
supabase_migrations_ledger is null: migrations are applied by hand in the SQL editor, so no ledger rows exist. That 0001-0014 are applied is inferred from schema shape, not recorded.

0015 and 0016 confirmed NOT applied: no save_household function, symptom_logs carries only symptom_logs_severity_check, full grants remain on the four locked tables, no home_contexts table, no daily_scores.home_context_id.

Production carries a SECURITY DEFINER function rls_auto_enable() returning event_trigger with search_path=pg_catalog. It is in no migration and no baseline. The audit does not read pg_event_trigger, so whether an event trigger is bound to it is unknown.
map_layers and water_snapshots have RLS enabled with no policies at all: service-role-only tables.
handle_new_user is SECURITY DEFINER with EXECUTE granted to anon and authenticated. It returns trigger so it cannot usefully be called directly, but the grant is unnecessary. Deferred hardening item.
Default privileges grant arwdDxtm on every new public table to anon and authenticated. 0016 correctly revokes these on home_contexts and re-grants only SELECT to authenticated.
_note: The full catalog JSON was reviewed in the session transcript rather than stored here, because it names every column of every table and is reproducible at any time by re-running docs/backend/baseline-audit.sql. Re-run it after applying 0015 and 0016 to capture the post-migration catalog.
